A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TropNNC work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison despite revisions and relocation.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original neural-network compression experiments, including classification accuracies, parameter counts, and FLOPs in Tables 1–6 and Figures 7–9.

after.justification: Section 7 retains original compression experiments and reports revised and additional empirical outcomes in Tables 1–7 and Figures 7–9.

M1.justification: Core Algorithms 1–3 remain. Section 6 extends non-uniform compression with two layer-specific threshold rules, scaling a global constant by either the square root of clustering-vector dimension or the mean vector norm. V1 used a global threshold without these adaptations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST digit pairs, full MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet. Linear-layer, convolutional-layer, and non-ReLU compression coverage remains. Fusion and threshold changes concern model configurations and evaluation procedures.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained: Zonotope and Neural Path K-means in the corresponding MNIST tables; Neural Path K-means, ThiNet, random structured pruning, and L1 structured pruning in Figures 7–9; and CUP in non-uniform comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 7 replaces v1's shared CUP clustering-vector control with comparisons using all TropNNC enhancements and revises non-uniform threshold settings. V2 separately evaluates fully fused models in Table 4 and reports original-network CUP versus layerwise-fused TropNNC comparisons in Tables 5–7. This substantially revises the non-uniform evaluation design.

E4.justification: V2 adds qualitative component-ablation and fusion-sensitivity findings, an iterative versus non-iterative VGG comparison, and analysis of the threshold variants' parameter/FLOP trade-offs. V1's shared-feature comparison isolating representative selection is replaced. The newly asserted component ablation lacks detailed numerical results.

E5.justification: Both versions retain plus/minus reporting in Tables 1–3, plotted error bars, and point estimates in the non-uniform tables. No new run counts, seeds, confidence-interval definitions, or statistical tests are reported. Changed error-bar magnitudes belong to concrete results.

E6.justification: Non-uniform results are extensively revised and expanded, including new fused-model Table 4. V1 Table 4 reports TropNNC at 79.84% with 3.42M VGG parameters; v2 Table 5 reports variant 1 at 93.21% with 3.53M under different settings, not a matched-setting gain. Figures 7–9 also revise baseline curves and error bars, notably strengthening L1 structured pruning in Figure 7b. Tables 1–3 retain their values.

T1.justification: The theorem statements and overall proof structure are retained, but mathematical errors are corrected. Appendix A.1 restores missing convex-combination coefficients; A.4 replaces an erroneous equality with a triangle-inequality bound. Appendices A.4 and A.6 also correctly describe comparison points rather than necessarily vertices.

C1.justification: The first contribution in Section 1 is narrowed from a tighter bound for tropical rational mappings to one for tropical polynomials. The principal compression and comparative-performance claims remain. Naming CUP in the abstract promotes a comparison already claimed in v1's introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V1 attributes the CUP advantage to representative selection; v2 attributes it to complementary enhancements. V2 explains the variants' parameter/FLOP trade-offs through their emphasis on later versus earlier layers and acknowledges that the benefit of pre-fusion clustering weights remains unexplained.

D1.justification: V2 provides experiment-specific fusion information, including fully fused VGG evaluation and layerwise fusion with pre-fusion clustering weights in non-uniform experiments. It identifies threshold variants and their settings more explicitly. Conversely, v1's explicit three-iteration designation for the ResNet56 comparison is not retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Tsilivis et al. (2022) and Kordonis et al. (2024) to the tropical-applications discussion. It also positions TropNNC as improving CUP's clustering-threshold step alongside features and representatives. Most other reference changes update metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract, distinguishes scalar tropical rational functions from vector mappings, renames Section 6, and expands selected explanatory paragraphs. The overall section sequence and most prose remain, so this is a limited revision rather than extensive restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adds a grouped multi-model Table 4 and expands the corresponding non-uniform tables with variant labels and rows. Experimental figures are relocated, with Figures 7 and 8 occupying figure-only pages. Captions are corrected, including Figure 8's identification of AlexNet linear layers and VGG convolutional layers.

improvement.justification: Corrected derivations in Appendix A and clearer fusion and threshold documentation provide a limited improvement in mathematical reliability and experimental interpretability. The benefit is tempered by replacing the shared-feature control with full-method comparisons while reporting the component ablation only qualitatively, which weakens attribution of the gains to individual enhancements.
